hero.headline: JetBlue ending Vero Beach to New York JFK route in September due to low demand
hero.teaser: JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as th
hero.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating in September. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates based on passenger numbers. "It's just the way that that market works, and air carriers will fluctuate based off of demand," Dambeck said. He added that JetBlue "just wasn't seeing what they were hoping for" with the New York route.

Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot at success. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time if given more opportunity. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked. I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. He noted the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach, saying, "It's easy. It's close." His comments reflect concerns from local travelers who appreciated having direct access to New York without driving to larger airports in South Florida or Orlando.

The Boston route continues to perform well at Vero Beach Regional Airport, with Dambeck saying "Boston is seeing great demand." Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time, demonstrating continued interest in that northeastern connection. The contrast between the two routes highlights how different markets can perform differently even when serving similar geographic regions. While both Boston and New York are major northeastern cities, the Boston service has attracted enough passengers to remain viable while the JFK route struggled to build a sustainable customer base.

Dambeck said the door is not closed on the JFK route returning in the future, noting "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back." This leaves open the possibility that JetBlue could restore service to New York if conditions change or demand increases. Airlines regularly reassess their route networks based on seasonal patterns, economic conditions, and shifting travel preferences. For now, Vero Beach travelers seeking to reach New York will need to connect through other cities or use alternative airports.

cards.headline: Two men killed in early morning shooting in Port St. Lucie neighborhood
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie Police Department is investigating a double fatal shooting that occurred early Sunday morning in a residential neighborhood. Officers responded around 3:30 a.m. to the 1300 block of Southeast Rivergreen Circle after receiving multiple 911 calls reporting gunshots. When officers arrived, they found two adult men suffering from multiple gunshot wounds in the driveways of a residence. Both victims were taken to separate local hospitals, where they later died from their injuries. Police identified the victims as Carl Loubeau, 24, and Juliun Stokes, 22.

Preliminary investigators believe some of the people involved had been socializing earlier in the evening before returning to a home on Southeast Rivergreen Circle. Police said a verbal altercation occurred outside the residence over a residential key and escalated into an exchange of gunfire between two of the individuals involved. Investigators believe the shooting was an isolated incident involving people who knew one another and said there is no ongoing threat to the public. All parties involved have either been detained or are cooperating with investigators, according to police.

Neighbor John Adams was working in his garage when the shooting occurred. "I was just working on my bicycle and I heard gunshots. Maybe two, three and I stayed in the garage and then I heard a girl screaming," Adams told WPTV reporter Zitlali Solache. He described a massive emergency response to the scene. "Every police officer in Port St. Lucie was here, there was twenty squads, two ambulances, two firetrucks, a helicopter. It was just mayhem," he said. Adams also said a police officer told him they photographed 16 casings at the scene. "Just devastating, terrible. My heart goes out to them," he said. Another neighbor who did not want to be identified told WPTV she dialed 911 and stayed with one of the wounded men until help arrived.

The investigation remains active as detectives continue conducting interviews, processing evidence and reviewing available information. Police said additional details, including any potential criminal charges, will be released as the investigation progresses. Anyone with information who has not yet spoken with detectives is asked to contact the Port St. Lucie Police Department.

cards.headline: Spain defeats Argentina 1-0 to win 2026 World Cup in extra time thriller
cards.body:
Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 on Sunday to win the 2026 FIFA World Cup championship. Ferran Torres scored the winning goal in the 106th minute of extra time, burying a left-footed shot just under the crossbar after pouncing on a bouncing ball in the box. It is Spain's second World Cup championship and first since 2010.

Spain was absolutely dominant throughout the match in terms of possession and shot attempts. The team took 15 shots in regulation while Argentina managed none. Spain also won nine corners compared to Argentina's single corner kick. Despite this overwhelming advantage, Lionel Messi and Argentina found a way to hang on and force the match into extra time. Torres broke through in the opening moment of the second 15-minute period of extra time to finally secure the victory for Spain.

Argentina's task became even more difficult when Enzo Fernandez was sent off in second-half stoppage time after receiving his second yellow card. Fernandez was carded for a reckless play that sent Spain defender Pau Cubarsi cartwheeling into the air, forcing Argentina to finish the match with only 10 players. About two minutes after play resumed, another foul gave Lamine Yamal a chance to seal the victory from about 22 yards out on a free kick. His curling strike toward the right post was saved by Argentina goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez, who made a diving stop for his 10th save of the afternoon, the most ever recorded in a World Cup final. Martinez leaped to his feet afterward, punching the air and encouraging the crowd to get loud before the match eventually went to extra time.

With the victory, Spain became the first nation to simultaneously hold the World Cup crowns in both men's and women's soccer. The final was the 104th and last match of the expanded 48-team tournament played across the United States, Canada and Mexico. Because there were more matches than any previous World Cup, the tournament produced 308 total goals, more than any other edition in history. According to FIFA, the 2026 World Cup was officially the most attended ever.

cards.headline: Snyder Drives in Five as St. Lucie Mets Hold Off Cardinals, 8-6
cards.teaser:
Trey Snyder delivered a career day at the plate Sunday as the St. Lucie Mets held off a late Palm Beach Cardinals rally for an 8-6 victory at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

Snyder
cards.body:
Trey Snyder delivered a career day at the plate Sunday as the St. Lucie Mets held off a late Palm Beach Cardinals rally for an 8-6 victory at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

Snyder went 4-for-5 with a home run, triple and five RBIs, helping St. Lucie win the three-game series two games to one.

After allowing the Cardinals to score first in each of the opening two games, the Mets took control with three runs in the first inning.

Randy Guzman opened the scoring with a 107 mph ground ball that Palm Beach third baseman Jonathan Mejia stopped but could not make a throw on, allowing Marco Vargas to score. Snyder followed with a two-run single that gave the Mets a 3-0 lead.

Starting pitcher Ethan Lanthier worked through early traffic and completed 2 1/3 scoreless innings. He allowed one hit and struck out four.

Tyler McLoughlin followed with 1 2/3 scoreless innings and earned the victory, improving his record to 2-2. McLoughlin has allowed only one earned run over his last 12 appearances and has now recorded six consecutive scoreless outings.

St. Lucie added three more runs in the third inning when Snyder launched his second home run of the season. The three-run shot brought home Mike Tauchman and Guzman and extended the Mets' advantage to 6-0.

Snyder continued his strong afternoon with a triple in the seventh inning. Branny De Oleo then hit his seventh home run of the season, a two-run shot that pushed St. Lucie's lead to 8-1.

Palm Beach made the game interesting in the bottom of the seventh.

Yairo Padilla hit his first home run of the season, a grand slam against Ernesto Mercedes, as the Cardinals scored five runs in the inning and cut the Mets' lead to 8-6.

Palm Beach brought the potential tying run to the plate in the ninth after Trevor Haskins was hit by a pitch. Miguel Mejias responded by striking out the next three batters to finish the game and earn his third save of the season.

St. Lucie pitchers combined for 17 strikeouts, marking the third consecutive game in which the Mets recorded double-digit strikeouts.

The Mets improved to 8-14 in the second half and 41-47 overall. Palm Beach fell to 13-10 in the second half and 65-43 overall.

St. Lucie will have an off day Monday before opening a new series against the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels on Tuesday. First pitch is scheduled for 6:05 p.m.

cards.headline: Safe Kids Treasure Coast offering free pool alarms to Martin County residents
cards.teaser: The Florida Department of Health and Safe Kids Treasure Coast are providing a limited supply of free pool alarms to qualifying Martin County residents with residential pools.
cards.body:
The Florida Department of Health and Safe Kids Treasure Coast are providing a limited supply of free pool alarms to qualifying Martin County residents with residential pools.

The program offers one alarm per household and has no income or priority group requirements, making it available to any qualifying resident regardless of financial status. The alarms are available while supplies last on a first-come, first-served basis, so interested residents should act promptly to secure one. Safe Kids Treasure Coast is asking residents to fill out an online survey to determine their eligibility for the program. For more information about the free pool alarm program, residents can call (772) 462-3501.

According to the coalition, a pool alarm serves as one layer of protection and should always be used alongside close adult supervision, pool barriers and water safety education to help prevent drowning. The program emphasizes that pool alarms are not a standalone safety solution but rather part of a comprehensive approach to water safety. Residents should note that a 9-volt battery is required to operate the alarm, but the battery is not included with the free alarm.

The initiative aims to increase water safety awareness and provide practical tools to help prevent drowning incidents in residential pools throughout Martin County. By distributing these alarms at no cost, the program seeks to remove financial barriers that might otherwise prevent families from implementing additional safety measures around their pools. The combination of free access and the comprehensive safety messaging demonstrates the coalition's commitment to protecting children and preventing water-related accidents in the community.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County residents adjust diets as E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks spread
cards.teaser: Health officials confirmed five local cases of cyclospora since May, including two in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County, prompting residents to change what they eat and avoid.
cards.body:
Reports of contaminated produce continue to spread across the country, and many people in South Florida are changing what they eat and what they avoid. The latest concern centers around lettuce linked to outbreaks of E. coli and cyclospora, including lettuce connected to Taco Bell locations. Health officials said thousands across the U.S. have been affected, with confirmed cases also reported locally from the Palm Beaches into the Treasure Coast.

According to the Florida Department of Health, there have been five confirmed local cases of cyclospora since May: two in Palm Beach County, two in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County. At restaurants, grocery stores and fast-food chains, some families say they are steering clear of leafy greens altogether. Dakota and Brynlee Rhodes, visiting Delray Beach with their mother Jenny, said they are trying to stay away from lettuce and stuff like that.

Samantha Barone, dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, said consumers should focus on produce with protective outer layers. Barone recommends sticking to melon and things that have a harder skin that you can peel. She also recommends washing all fruits and vegetables thoroughly before eating them and says beans and nuts are safe alternatives that still provide fiber and protein. Barone recommends cleaning produce using a 1-to-3 part mixture of distilled white vinegar and water.

cards.headline: Major League Baseball restricts dugout iPad use to prevent AI from making decisions
cards.teaser: MLB made custom tabs on dugout iPads inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday to stop artificial intelligence from being used for in-game decisions traditionally made by players and coaches.
cards.body:
Major League Baseball is restricting iPad usage in dugouts to prevent the tablets from running artificial intelligence to help make decisions. MLB made the custom tabs inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday night, when the second half of the season started. The tablets have access to video and league-provided data, and also included a custom tab where teams could access other programs.

MLB executive vice president of baseball operations Morgan Sword wrote in a June 11 memo to general managers, assistant GMs and video coordinators that in many cases, the custom tab had expanded the use of the dugout iPads beyond their originally intended purpose to include recommendations regarding substitutions, pitch calling, and other in-game decisions traditionally made by players and coaches. A review by the competition committee found clubs had been compliant with the regulations. MLB started a pilot program allowing use of iPads in dugouts with restrictions late in the 2015 season and expanded their use in 2016 under a deal with Apple. Video was eliminated in the 2020 COVID season following the Houston Astros' sign-stealing scandal, then returned in 2021.

cards.headline: Britain's Josh Kerr breaks mile world record with 3:42.66 run in London
cards.teaser: Josh Kerr shattered a 27-year-old world record on Saturday, running the mile in 3:42.66 at a Diamond League event in London.
cards.body:
Great Britain's Josh Kerr ran the mile in 3:42.66 on Saturday in London, breaking Hicham El Guerrouj's previous mark of 3:43.13 set in 1999. The 27-year-old made no secret that he was targeting the long-standing record at Saturday's Diamond League event in London. Earlier this week, he revealed he ran 2:42.45 in a 1,200-meter time trial. His sponsor, Brooks, dubbed the effort "Project 222," referencing the number of seconds in 3 minutes, 42 seconds. American Yared Nuguse finished second in 3:45.69.

Kerr has emerged as one of the world's top middle-distance runners, winning bronze in the 1,500 meters at the Tokyo Olympics and silver at the 2024 Paris Olympics. Before turning professional, Kerr starred at the University of New Mexico, where he won multiple NCAA titles. He also set an NCAA indoor mile record of 3:35.01 in 2018. Kerr's record-setting run came during the Diamond League, an established international circuit of professional track and field events.

cards.headline: World Cup final security includes Secret Service perimeter with President Trump attending
cards.teaser: Federal agents, local law enforcement and private companies continue security preparations for Sunday's Argentina-Spain World Cup final in New Jersey, with a Secret Service perimeter in place for President Trump's attendance.
cards.body:
The World Cup final Sunday in New Jersey will include a beefed-up Secret Service perimeter, with President Trump attending the trophy presentation. The final is a Level 1 Special Event, the highest possible security designation, with added resources from the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Defense, and the FBI. White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt says his attendance will cap what has been the most watched, most secure, and most successful World Cup in American history. When Trump attended an NBA Finals game last month in New York, police shut down several city blocks around the arena and fans were forced to wait in extra-long lines to go through enhanced security.

A joint operations center in New York has helped oversee security and monitor threats in host cities throughout the tournament, with thousands of personnel on the ground and a team with an eye on the skies. The FBI has seized hundreds of drones flying in restricted airspace near stadiums during the tournament. FBI Special Agent Adam Kachhia-Patel says agents will be getting live feeds and monitoring any drone activity in the area to see if there is anything that needs to be addressed from a threat perspective. No one will be allowed to simply walk up to the stadium or drive a personal vehicle. Those with a ticket must take approved transportation to the game and should arrive early to make their way through the stepped-up security.

cards.headline: Messi bathed Yamal as baby in 2007 photo shoot, now they meet in World Cup final
cards.teaser: A 2007 charity calendar photo shoot paired teenage Lionel Messi with infant Lamine Yamal. Now 19 years later, they face off in Sunday's World Cup final.
cards.body:
Photographer Joan Monfort took photos in 2007 of a teenage Lionel Messi bathing infant Lamine Yamal in a plastic bathtub as part of a charity calendar produced by local newspaper Sport and UNICEF. Monfort, who works as a freelance photojournalist for The Associated Press, took the photos after Yamal's mother won a raffle of families in the city of Mataró near Barcelona who wanted to participate. Soccer destiny paired her baby boy with the Argentine who would become the greatest of all time. Messi left Barcelona in 2021 when the club was in financial trouble. Yamal erupted at the club two years later.

Monfort had no recollection of the photos until Yamal's father posted one on social media during the 2024 European Championship, when a teenage Yamal led Spain to the title. The photo went viral then, but interest has skyrocketed with Sunday's World Cup final between Argentina and Spain approaching. Monfort said he has been bombarded by queries for the photos by professional media outlets while also seeing his images reproduced countless times on social media and the internet without any credit or compensation. The 19-year-old Yamal will face a Messi who is 20 years his senior in Sunday's final. Monfort, 58, is considering traveling to see the final in New Jersey. He said his heart is split and he does not know if he wants Messi or Yamal to win.

hero.headline: Boca Raton TLC Program Offers Summer Service Projects for South Florida Families
hero.teaser: B'nai Torah Congregation's TLC Program connects volunteers with hands-on service projects ranging from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking and literacy efforts.
hero.body:
B'nai Torah Congregation's TLC Program is offering South Florida families a range of hands-on service projects this summer, from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking, literacy efforts and care for seniors. Led by Summer Faerman, the program connects volunteers of all ages with mitzvah opportunities, or meaningful good deeds, as part of the congregation's broader community outreach efforts.

The TLC Program stands for Tzedakah, Learning and Chesed, and has made service a central part of synagogue life since 2012. The program provides a way for individuals and families to put Jewish values into action while helping people in need across South Florida. It addresses multiple community concerns including hunger, homelessness, literacy, elder care, vulnerable populations and special needs. Organizers emphasize that the projects are open to everyone in the community, not only members of B'nai Torah Congregation, with the goal of making service practical, welcoming and easy to begin.

Participants can volunteer in various ways throughout the summer. Projects include making sandwiches, serving meals, collecting and cleaning shoes, stocking Little Free Pantries, preparing backpacks for back-to-school efforts, creating Bags of Hope and helping seniors with technology. Organizers plan to demonstrate volunteer projects such as wrapping presents, making flower arrangements, preparing sandwiches, collecting shoes and assembling supplies for people in need. The variety of options allows families to choose activities that match their interests and schedules.

As summer continues, the TLC Program offers families a way to stay connected, teach children about giving back and support neighbors throughout South Florida. B'nai Torah Congregation says the program is built around the idea that small acts of service can strengthen the larger community. More information about the TLC Program is available through B'nai Torah Congregation's website.

hero.headline: Florida Falls Outside Top Five Most Retirement-Friendly States in New National Ranking
hero.teaser: Florida failed to secure a position among the top five most retirement-friendly states in a new national ranking released Sunday, challenging the state's long-held reputation as a
hero.body:
Florida failed to secure a position among the top five most retirement-friendly states in a new national ranking released Sunday, challenging the state's long-held reputation as a premier retirement destination. The assessment from Moneywise evaluated states based on factors affecting retirees' quality of life and financial security. The ranking represents a shift in how retirement destinations are evaluated across the United States, excluding a state that has traditionally dominated conversations about ideal places to spend retirement years.

Florida has traditionally marketed itself as an ideal location for retirees, with its warm climate and lack of state income tax serving as major draws for older Americans. The state's senior population has grown substantially over decades, with retirees from northeastern and midwestern states relocating to Florida communities in significant numbers. However, the new analysis considered multiple factors that affect retirement living, including cost of living, healthcare access, tax structures, and overall quality of life indicators. The exclusion of Florida from the top five suggests that other locations now offer more attractive combinations of affordability and amenities for retirees.

Florida has faced rising property insurance costs, increased housing prices, and higher overall living expenses in recent years, factors that may have influenced its position in the ranking. These economic pressures have created new challenges for retirees on fixed incomes who must balance the appeal of warm weather and outdoor lifestyles against escalating costs of maintaining their standard of living. Despite these financial headwinds, the findings arrive as Florida continues to see substantial population growth, with many new residents arriving at or near retirement age. The state's economy remains heavily dependent on retiree spending and the industries that support senior populations, including healthcare, real estate, and leisure services.

How this ranking affects future retirement migration patterns to Florida remains uncertain, though the state's established retirement communities and infrastructure continue to attract older Americans seeking warmer climates and outdoor lifestyles. The ranking signals that retirees now have compelling alternatives to consider when choosing their retirement destinations, potentially reshaping demographic trends that have favored Florida for generations. While the specific states that ranked in the top five were not detailed in the available information, Florida's absence from the list marks a notable development for a state whose identity and economy have been closely tied to its status as a retirement haven.

hero.headline: Two Martin County brush fires contained, more expected this summer
hero.teaser: Martin County saw two brush fires this week, including one sparked by a lightning strike, both now fully contained and being monitored by the Florida Forest Service.
hero.body:
Two brush fires broke out in Martin County this week, including one ignited by a lightning strike, and both are now fully contained and under monitoring by the Florida Forest Service. Officials are warning that conditions favorable for brush fires will continue throughout the summer months as the region remains in peak fire season.

David Grubitch, a mitigation specialist and spokesperson with the Florida Forest Service, said summertime heat is drying out fine dead fuels, making them highly receptive when lightning strikes occur. However, he emphasized that residents should not be alarmed by these conditions, as they are typical for this time of year. Grubitch explained that while rain often extinguishes fires immediately after they start, some fires can travel underground and resurface days later, making them more difficult to detect and contain.

The Florida Forest Service is relying on public assistance to help monitor and respond to brush fires quickly. Grubitch stressed that residents play a crucial role in helping the department do its job effectively and urged people to never assume someone else has already reported a brush fire they spot. He emphasized the importance of immediate notification, saying that if residents see something, they should say something, as it can make all the difference in how quickly crews are able to get a fire under control. Quick reporting remains one of the most effective tools in preventing small fires from becoming larger, more dangerous blazes that threaten homes and natural areas.

With summer conditions expected to continue creating favorable environments for brush fires, the Florida Forest Service will maintain its heightened monitoring and response efforts throughout the season. The department continues to track contained fires and remains prepared to respond to new incidents as they arise. Residents are encouraged to remain vigilant and report any signs of smoke or fire to local authorities immediately, regardless of whether they believe others may have already called it in. Officials stress that multiple reports of the same fire are preferable to a fire going unreported and potentially spreading out of control.

hero.headline: Unity in the Community event connects Fort Pierce families with police and services

hero.headline: JetBlue ending Vero Beach to New York JFK route in September due to low demand
hero.teaser: JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as th
hero.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating in September. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates based on passenger numbers. "It's just the way that that market works, and air carriers will fluctuate based off of demand," Dambeck said. He added that JetBlue "just wasn't seeing what they were hoping for" with the New York route.

Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot at success. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time if given more opportunity. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked. I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. He noted the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach, saying, "It's easy. It's close." His comments reflect concerns from local travelers who appreciated having direct access to New York without driving to larger airports in South Florida or Orlando.

The Boston route continues to perform well at Vero Beach Regional Airport, with Dambeck saying "Boston is seeing great demand." Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time, demonstrating continued interest in that northeastern connection. The contrast between the two routes highlights how different markets can perform differently even when serving similar geographic regions. While both Boston and New York are major northeastern cities, the Boston service has attracted enough passengers to remain viable while the JFK route struggled to build a sustainable customer base.

Dambeck said the door is not closed on the JFK route returning in the future, noting "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back." This leaves open the possibility that JetBlue could restore service to New York if conditions change or demand increases. Airlines regularly reassess their route networks based on seasonal patterns, economic conditions, and shifting travel preferences. For now, Vero Beach travelers seeking to reach New York will need to connect through other cities or use alternative airports.
